A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that a beamlike field can be represented in terms of a sum of plane waves, and that the scattering of this field from a sphere is the same as the scattering of the plane wave components.

, in general, the exact solution for the scattering of a beam from a sphere is a linear combination of the exact solution for plane-wave scattering from a sphere and a term that represents a beamlike component.
we have provided an exact, rigorous formulation of the scattering problem, which is applicable to any incident radiation field and to any sphere.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the scattering of beam fields from spheres is not a new phenomenon, but rather is the same as that of plane waves, and that the "forward scattering" of beam fields is not a new concept, but is simply the scattering of beam-like fields into a forward direction.
the exact formulation for the forward scattering of a Gaussian field by a nonabsoring sphere is given by the sum of the Mie scattering coefficients for the incident and scattered waves.

, in the case of a beamlike field, there exists a unique solution for the scattering of the field by a sphere, and that solution is given by the exact formulation of the forward scattering of the beamlike field by the sphere.
